A convergence zone between the monsoon westerlies and east trade
winds is setting up right over the Marianas tonight as widespread 
showers and isolated thunderstorms are now expected over Guam with a 
potential for locally heavy rainfall. Precipitation chances will
decrease north of Guam, remaining scattered over Tinian and Saipan.
The convergence zone is expected to move out of the area by tomorrow
morning and be replaced with scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms. Lower cloud coverage and light winds over Tinian and
Saipan could allow for island effect showers and thunderstorms over 
the southern portion of Saipan. Light and variable winds Tuesday
morning will allow for island effect showers and thunderstorms to 
develop over Guam, Tinian, and Saipan, likely pushing south as a
north wind begins to move into the area. Depending on the track and
intensity of Invest 92W, another convergence zone may develop Tuesday
night. Afterwards, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are
expected most days for the rest of the forecast period. However, a
fair amount of uncertainty remains due to 92W.

Marine...
Gentle southwesterlies are expected across the Marianas tonight
before decreasing to light to gentle tomorrow, and then light and
variable by Monday. A faster weakening of the monsoon trough to the 
west has dropped combined seas slightly to 4 to 6 feet and this is 
expected to remain steady before possibly decreasing slightly by 
Tuesday. A moderate risk of rip currents continues for the next few 
days along south, west, and north-facing reefs. There is a moderate 
risk of lightning through the week. A surge of moisture from the 
east bring widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms for Guam 
coastal waters with shower coverage decreasing to the north and 
becoming scattered over Tinian and Saipan. More bands of scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms will be possible throughout the 
week depending on the development and track of Invest 92W in eastern 
Micronesia. This system will continue to be monitored closely.

Tropical Systems...
A developing disturbance, Invest 92W, is centered north-northeast of
Pohnpei near 10N157E. The invest lies within a broad west to east
oriented trough. Latest satellite data shows a weak Low-Level
Circulation Center (LLCC) with some convection near the center. The
strongest convection lies along the trough to the west and within a
band of convergence south of the trough and invest across Chuuk,
Pohnpei and Kosrae States to south of Majuro. Guidance shows the
system moving slowly west-northwest, then turning northwest toward
the far northern CNMI late in the week. There is a large degree of
uncertainty with Invest 92W. However, the general consensus is for
gradual development as 92W moves toward the northern CNMI. The Joint
Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) has rated Invest 92W as low, meaning 
development is unlikely during the next 24 hours. Residents of the 
Marianas should continue to monitor forecasts for any changes to the 
expected evolution of Invest 92W.

For more information on Invest 92W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Another weak circulation, newly formed Invest 94W, is centered well
north of Yap near 18N136E. Although 94W is currently rated sub-low,
meaning no development is expected over the next few days, model 
guidance has shown this region is favorable for development. invest
94W is not expected to affect the Marianas or Micronesia as it moves
easst-northeast to northeast over the next few days.

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 92W remains and the associated trough remain active across
eastern Micronesia today. Latest 925mb analysis shows that this
trough is very close to becoming the primary monsoon trough, with
weak troughing now seen from Invest 93W (north of 25N) to Invest 92W.
92W has become a bit more organized, resulting in it being upgraded
from sub-low to low. As the trough strengthens and replaces the
monsoon trough farther north, this will feed more energy into 
Invest 92W as it moves northwest, with strong convergence continuing
south of the trough where a southerly push will continue to cross the
Equator and converge with the monsoonal flow. This will maintain an
active pattern across the region for the next several days. Kosrae
and Pohnpei can expect brief periods of little or no showers with
periods of numerous to widespread locally heavy showers and isolated
thunderstorms through the middle of the week. Heavy rainfall capable
of producing flash flooding and mudslides remains a threat for the
next few days. By the end of the week, Kosrae, then Pohnpei, can
expect to see a drier pattern for a couple of days. 

For Majuro, the developing monsoon trough will be the main player,
bringing a couple periods of numerous locally heavy showers and 
isolated thunderstorms to the Marshalls Monday into Monday night.
